newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Proton, other motor stocks down.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Proton, other motor stocks down.

text.p: Malaysian motor stocks fell on Monday due to concerns that the rise of the yen will cut into the companies' profits, analysts and dealers said.
At the midday break, national carmaker Proton Bhd was down 1.10 ringgit to 13.60 and car distributor EON by 20 cents to 24.60. The stock of their parent company Hicom Holdings was down 30 to 5.05.

Malaysian car makers and assemblers are particularly sensitive to yen fluctuations because a larger portion of their car parts are imported from Japan. A stronger Japanese currency would increase the cost of the parts.
The stocks of distributors of Japanese cars in Malaysia also fell.
Tan Chong Motor fell 22 cents to 4.48, Oriental Holdings by 80 to 18.80 and UMW Holdings by 70 to 12.40.
"The import cost goes up and if you can't pass it on to your customer, that cuts into your margins," said Jupiter Securities' institutional dealer Tony Shue.
Added an equity salesman at Jardine Fleming: "All the motor stocks are yen-sensitive, as the parts are from Japan, especially Proton."
The yen has risen about 6.3 percent against the ringgit in the last two weeks to track movements of the dollar/yen.
Around 0500 GMT, a ringgit was quoted at 2.1066/88 per 100 yen.
The yen fell to a four-month low against the dollar in New York last Friday.
Dealers cited a reversal in expectations for U.S. and Japanese interest rates as well as repeated jawboning by Japanese officials for deflating the dollar.
